item.strong: SRS v1 · Bank Customer Onboarding System with Dual KYC Approval

srs.title: Bank Customer Onboarding System with Dual KYC Approval
srs.summary: Develop a web-based application to facilitate new customer onboarding. The system must enforce dual approval by both an Onboarding Officer and a Compliance Officer before an account is activated. It must integrate with the existing Customer Management System (CMS) to create the customer profile and,
assumptions: The client has an existing, accessible Customer Management System (CMS) capable of receiving integration via API.
A live, stable interface with the Customer KYC Repository (CKYCR) is available during the UAT and Production phases.
The organization's HR system has defined the list of 'Onboarding Staff' and 'Compliance Staff' with specific user IDs.
Standard banking infrastructure (identity management, document storage service, audit logging service) is available for consumption by the new application.
stakeholders: Onboarding Staff (perform initial data entry and document upload).
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Staff (may be required for manual escalation if the automated workflow fails).
System Administrator (manages user access and system configuration).
Compliance Officer (supervisory role for approving exceptions or high-risk cases).

findings.text: Approval Workflow Granularity. The brief specifies 'dual approval' but the user answers to Q1 ('Who must approve new onboarding requests?') were skipped. It is unclear if these approvals must happen '

Authentication Mechanism. The brief mentions 'secure' authentication but no method was selected. The user answers to Q2 were skipped. Evidence E2 suggests Aadhaar e-KYC or DigiLocker might be expected
Document Limits. The brief mentions 'secure document storage' but the user answers to Q3 ('What is the maximum file size...') were skipped. Evidence E2 mentions offline Aadhaar verification requires

risks.title: Regulatory Compliance Risk (PMLA 2002)
risks.text: The brief mentions 'KYC verification' but does not explicitly reference the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The provided evidence (E1, E2, E5) contains strict regulatory requirements (e.g.,

openIssues: Confirm the specific roles and approval hierarchy for the dual approval process (e.g., sequential vs. parallel, specific job titles).
Define the required authentication method (e.g., SSO, MFA, Aadhaar-based) as per internal security policy and Evidence E2.

Set the technical constraints for document uploads (Maximum file size in KB/MB, supported formats like PDF/JPG), as Evidence E2 implies Aadhaar XML files which are likely larger than standard documents.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the onboarding of up to 10,000 concurrent customers, with performance metrics ensuring sub-2-second response times for KYC verification queries.
requirements.acceptance: Load testing with 10,000 simulated users and 100 concurrent query batches demonstrates <2s latency under peak load conditions.

requirements.statement: The system shall implement a dual-approval workflow where onboarding requests require distinct authorization from both an onboarding staff member and a compliance staff member before account creation.
requirements.acceptance: System logic enforces state transition to 'Approved' only after two unique user approvals from distinct role groups (Onboarding Admin, Compliance Officer) within a 4-hour window.

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with the existing Customer Management System (CMS) to bi-directionally sync new customer profiles and approved KYC records via a secure API gateway.
requirements.acceptance: Successfully executed API handshake test confirming 100% data synchronization of new profiles and KYC status updates within 5 minutes of final approval.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow Retrieval Entities (REs) to fetch KYC records from the Central KYC Registry (CKYCR) using a KYC Identifier, restricting the requirement for customers to submit original physical
requirements.acceptance: User journey test confirms the system automatically populates 95% of required KYC fields from CKYCR fetch, only prompting the customer to upload documents when specific exceptions

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce redaction or blacking out of sensitive Personal Identifiable Information (PII), specifically Aadhaar numbers, in all displayed and stored documentation.
requirements.acceptance: Automated scan of 100 random audit logs and document renders confirms zero instances of visible Aadhaar numbers or unmasked PII columns.

requirements.statement: The system shall record a complete, immutable audit trail for all KYC updates and retrievals, including the exact timestamp of the data push to CKYCR, which must occur within seven days of receiving
requirements.acceptance: Audit log analysis confirms 100% of 'Update KYC' and 'Push to CKYCR' events are logged with timestamps; manual verification shows 100% of system-generated push events occur <7 days

requirements.statement: The system shall capture and store both audio-video interaction data and a photograph of the customer during virtual identification processes to verify interaction liveness.
requirements.acceptance: Database schema includes fields for 'video_path' and 'photo_path'; playback module successfully streams video content with frame rate >15fps and allows photo extraction.

requirements.statement: The system shall block the onboarding workflow if the customer's identity appears on any government-maintained negative list or if the customer is flagged as a previously rejected case.
requirements.acceptance: Integration test with negative list API returns a 'Rejected' status and halts the workflow if the customer's identifier is found in the active negative list feed.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a notification mechanism to customers with incomplete or lapsed KYC records, containing clear instructions and an escalation path, with the first notice sent no later than 30
requirements.acceptance: System generates reminder emails/SMS within 30 days of KYC lapse date; test environment verifies the inclusion of 'consequences of failure' and 'help contacts' in the template.

requirements.statement: The system shall restrict the duration of the dual-approval workflow and prohibit any onboarding request remaining in 'Pending Approval' state for more than 48 hours, triggering an automatic status re
requirements.acceptance: Automated timeout trigger executes at 48 hours (8 business cycles) for any pending request, changing status to 'Timed Out' and notifying supervisors.

traceability.check: Load testing with 10,000 simulated users and 100 concurrent query batches demonstrates <2s latency under peak load conditions
System logic enforces state transition to 'Approved' only after two unique user approvals from distinct role groups (Onboarding Admin, Compliance Officer) within a 4-hour window
Successfully executed API handshake test confirming 100% data synchronization of new profiles and KYC status updates within 5 minutes of final approval
User journey test confirms the system automatically populates 95% of required KYC fields from CKYCR fetch, only prompting the customer to upload documents when specific exceptions
Automated scan of 100 random audit logs and document renders confirms zero instances of visible Aadhaar numbers or unmasked PII columns
Audit log analysis confirms 100% of 'Update KYC' and 'Push to CKYCR' events are logged with timestamps
Database schema includes fields for 'video_path' and 'photo_path'
Integration test with negative list API returns a 'Rejected' status and halts the workflow if the customer's identifier is found in the active negative list feed
System generates reminder emails/SMS within 30 days of KYC lapse date
Automated timeout trigger executes at 48 hours (8 business cycles) for any pending request, changing status to 'Timed Out' and notifying supervisors
